result.title: VLA-Retain: Benchmarking Cross-Dimension Effects of Vision Tuning in VLAs
result.summary: Vision-language-action (VLA) models transfer knowledge from large-scale pretraining into robot control, but their manipulation performance remains sensitive to changes in observation conditions, which recent work addresses by fine-tuning the visual module on target-domain data. However, it remains unclear how such adaptation affects robustness beyond the target condition, as existing robustness benchmarks only evaluate models without fine-tuning and adaptation studies only report the target gain. Measuring this cross-dimension effect requires separating target gains from off-target changes, isolating adaptation effects from architectural differences, ruling out generic forgetting, and comparing tuning choices. Therefore, we introduce VLA-Retain, a benchmark that compares five open VLA models, tuned on Camera-view or Sensor-noise data, with their own base checkpoints on LIBERO-Plus dataset spanning seven perturbation dimensions. Our study reveals four findings. First, targeted vision tuning is not local, and its target gain does not predict retention. Mean off-target gain is negative in 8 of 10 model--domain configurations. Under Camera-view tuning, X-VLA gains $69.4$ percentage points on the target but loses $4.6$ points on average elsewhere, whereas OpenVLA-OFT gains $39.3$ and $1.4$ points, respectively. Second, these regressions are not explained only by performance loss on the same tasks without perturbations. Third, broader training coverage raises overall gain over target-specific training but does not eliminate dimension-level regressions. Fourth, tuning strategies are model-dependent, as DELTA-style feature preservation raises X-VLA's mean off-target gain to $+1.2$ points but lowers OpenVLA-OFT's to $-23.1$. Overall, these findings show that target-domain success alone is insufficient and highlight cross-dimensional retention as a key criterion for targeted VLA adaptation.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 VLA-Retain 基准，在 LIBERO-Plus 的七个扰动维度上，将五个开源 VLA 模型经相机视角或传感器噪声数据视觉微调后的表现与各自基座对比，以分离目标增益与非目标维度的变化；发现目标增益不能预测保留，10 组模型–域配置中 8 组跨维度平均为负，且广度训练与特征保持策略的效果依模型而异。
AI.relevance_reason: 直接对应「视觉细节与任务必要信息是否保留在内部状态」的问题：该基准显示针对性视觉微调会造成非目标视觉维度退化，可供核查 LVR 中视觉旁路与信息坍缩，其分离目标增益、通用遗忘与架构差异的评测设计也可能迁移到 latent 状态保留度诊断；但与推理期 latent 生成无直接关系，需核查。
